intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that nanophthalmos-4 (NNO4) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TMEM98 gene (615949) on chromosome 17q11.2.

paragraphs.text: Nanophthalmos-4 is an autosomal dominant eye disorder in which the eyes are small, with a short axial length, and there is high hyperopia without other physical anomalies (Yu et al., 2009; Awadalla et al., 2014; Khorram et al., 2015). Angle-closure glaucoma has been reported in older affected individuals (Yu et al., 2009).

checks.evidence_quote: Microphthalmia was inherited in an autosomal dominant manner in this family.
checks.explanation: Paper describes AD simple microphthalmia in this family.

checks.claim: In nanophthalmos-4 the eyes are small with a short axial length.
checks.evidence_quote: Simple microphthalmia (OMIM 309700), which refers to a structurally normal but small eye globe
checks.explanation: Small eye with short axial length (mean 19.29 mm) described.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos-4 features high hyperopia.
checks.evidence_quote: An unusually high incidence of high hyperopia and frequent occurrence of angle-closure glaucoma were noted.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos-4 occurs without other physical anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: All family members did not have any other physical anomalies.

checks.evidence_quote: Angle-closure glaucoma or occludable anterior chamber angles were present in three patients who were all older than 50 years of age

paragraphs.text: Yu et al. (2009) described a 5-generation Chinese family with isolated (simple) microphthalmia inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. The 9 affected members were aged 6 to 66 years. All had bilateral hyperopia ranging from +4.50 to +11.50 diopters (mean +8.00) and short axial length of 18.22 to 20.26 mm (mean 19.29 mm). Best corrected visual acuity was less than 0.5 in most eyes, and no family member had any other physical anomaly. Three patients, all older than 50 years, had angle-closure glaucoma or occludable anterior chamber angles. The glaucoma was treated by trabeculectomy but kept progressing, and 2 patients eventually developed atrophia bulbi despite repeated surgeries. The authors also noted learning disabilities in one-third of the cases. On histologic examination of sclera from affected members, the collagen fibers were diffusely swollen, twisted or frayed, and mixed with normal fibers. In the 2 atrophied globes, collagen alignment was disrupted, the sclera contained coil-like amorphous material and was 3 times normal thickness, and the cornea was also thickened.

paragraphs.text: Awadalla et al. (2014) studied a large white family (NNO-SA1), recruited in South Australia, with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos. Nanophthalmos was defined as an axial length less than 20.0 mm and/or a refractive error greater than +7.00. Of 35 available family members, 16 (46%) had nanophthalmos, with a mean refraction of +11.8 D and a mean axial length of 17.6 mm.

paragraphs.text: In the Chinese family with autosomal dominant microphthalmia that they studied, Yu et al. (2009) found a normal karyotype in all affected members. Two-point linkage analysis with 23 microsatellite markers produced lod scores below 1 for every marker, excluding linkage to CHX10, PAX6, MFRP and to the loci on 14q32, 11p, and 2q11-q14. paragraphs.text: In affected members of the white family (NNO-SA1) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos linked to 17p12-q12, Awadalla et al. (2014) used exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous missense mutation (c.577G-C; A193P) in exon 8 of the TMEM98 gene. It was the only novel segregating variant within the linked region and was absent from the Exome Variant Server and from 285 local white controls. Using RT-PCR, Awadalla et al. (2014) found that TMEM98 was expressed in all ocular tissues tested, including the sclera and the optic nerve head. The authors concluded that TMEM98 most likely causes the disease in this family.

paragraphs.text: In the US family (pedigree 991-F) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos, Khorram et al. (2015) performed exome sequencing of an affected member and found 4 nonsynonymous variants in the linked chromosome 17 region. Only a heterozygous missense mutation in TMEM98 (H196P) cosegregated with nanophthalmos and was predicted to be pathogenic by SIFT, PolyPhen, and BLOSUM62. In the Mariana Islands family (pedigree 951-N), Khorram et al. (2015) used Sanger sequencing to identify a heterozygous 34-bp deletion in TMEM98 in all 11 affected members tested; the deletion was absent from healthy family members.

checks.explanation: The prose supports the claim, but Table 3 marks SLC47A1 Ile414Thr as 'Yes' for co-inheritance as well, so H196P is unique only on the combined criteria. The paper also never says H196P is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 H196P mutation was predicted to be pathogenic by SIFT, PolyPhen, and BLOSUM62.
checks.evidence_quote: The TMEM98 missense mutation in pedigree 991-F, His196Pro, produced a BLOSUM62 score of −2, a PolyPhen score of 0.998 (probably damaging), and a SIFT score of 0 (damaging).

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a large white family from South Australia (NNO-SA1) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos, Awadalla et al. (2014) identified a heterozygous c.577G-C transversion in exon 8 of the TMEM98 gene, resulting in an ala193-to-pro (A193P) substitution. The mutation, found by exome sequencing, was the only novel segregating variant within the linked 17p12-q12 region and was absent from the Exome Variant Server and from 285 local white controls.

checks.claim: Awadalla et al. (2014) identified a heterozygous c.577G-C transversion in exon 8 of the TMEM98 gene in affected members of family NNO-SA1, a large white family from South Australia with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.evidence_quote: located in exon 8 of the transmembrane-98 (TMEM98) gene c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro)
checks.explanation: The variant, exon and family description match the abstract, but the abstract does not state that the variant is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 c.577G-C transversion results in an ala193-to-pro (A193P) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro)
checks.explanation: p.Ala193Pro is the same substitution as A193P, and a G>C change is a transversion.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 A193P mutation was found by exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region
checks.explanation: The abstract states the variant was found by exome sequencing.

checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region
checks.explanation: The abstract states it was the only novel segregating variant, and the title gives the region as 17p12-q12.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 A193P mutation was absent from the Exome Variant Server and from 285 local white controls.
checks.evidence_quote: which was absent in the Exome Variant Server database and among 285 local white individuals serving as controls
checks.explanation: Both absences are stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: In a Caucasian family of German heritage living in the United States (pedigree 991-F) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos, Khorram et al. (2015) identified a heterozygous his196-to-pro (H196P) mutation in the TMEM98 gene by exome sequencing. Of 4 nonsynonymous variants in the linked chromosome 17 region, only this mutation cosegregated with nanophthalmos and was predicted to be pathogenic by SIFT, PolyPhen, and BLOSUM62. The mutation affects a highly conserved histidine and was absent from the Exome Variant Server and 1000 Genomes Project databases.

checks.claim: Khorram et al. (2015) identified a heterozygous his196-to-pro (H196P) mutation in TMEM98 by exome sequencing in pedigree 991-F, a Caucasian family of German heritage living in the United States with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.evidence_quote: Genes within these "linked regions" were examined for disease-causing mutations using exome sequencing, and a His196Pro mutation was detected in the TMEM98 gene
checks.explanation: H196P found by exome sequencing in 991-F, but the paper does not state that it is heterozygous.

checks.claim: Of 4 nonsynonymous variants in the linked chromosome 17 region in pedigree 991-F, only TMEM98 H196P cosegregated with nanophthalmos.

checks.explanation: Table 3 marks SLC47A1 Ile414Thr as co-inherited with disease ('Yes') too. H196P is unique only on the combined criteria.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 H196P mutation was predicted to be pathogenic by SIFT, PolyPhen, and BLOSUM62.
checks.evidence_quote: The TMEM98 missense mutation in pedigree 991-F, His196Pro, produced a BLOSUM62 score of −2, a PolyPhen score of 0.998 (probably damaging), and a SIFT score of 0 (damaging).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 H196P mutation affects a highly conserved histidine.
checks.evidence_quote: The His196Pro mutation detected in pedigree 991-F alters a histidine amino acid that is highly conserved across many disparate species
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.evidence_quote: Neither the His196Pro mutation nor the 34 bp deletion was detected in public DNA sequence databases including the Exome Variation Server and the 1000 Genomes Project.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: In all 11 affected members tested of a Pacific Islander family of Micronesian heritage from the Mariana Islands (pedigree 951-N) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos, Khorram et al. (2015) identified by Sanger sequencing a heterozygous 34-bp deletion in the TMEM98 gene (c.694_721delAGAATGAAGACTGGATCGAAGATGCCTCgtaagg). The deletion spans the last 28 bp of exon 4 and the first 6 bp of intron 4, eliminates a splice site, and results in premature termination of translation. It was absent from healthy family members and from public databases.
